plate_findings.evidence: caption: (Left): Orange tonsils; in-text: orange-colored tonsils (Figure 1—left)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (Left, Middle, Right). Left: Left panel is a clinical photograph of the patient's oropharynx showing orange-yellow enlarged tonsils, a classic manifestation of Tangier disease described in the article. Middle: Middle panel is a clinical photograph of the patient's distended abdomen, consistent with the reported massive hepatosplenomegaly. No exact Tangier-disease finding key is in the provided vocabulary, so the visible manifestation is proposed. Right: Right panel shows the patient's hands with digital clubbing, mentioned in the physical examination in the setting of genetically confirmed Tangier disease. Clubbing is nonspecific and not a classic Tangier-disease manifestation; attribution is therefore low-confidence.

in_text_mentions: Physical examination: mild blood pressure elevation, BMI within the normal range, yellowing of sclera, orange-colored tonsils (Figure 1—left), red-colored and intensely itchy nodules on the nape of the neck (diagnosed as prurigo nodularis of Hyde), aortic and mitral stenosis murmurs, distended abdomen with massive hepatosplenomegaly (Figure 1—middle), umbilical hernia, vascular murmurs at both femoral arteries, clubbing (Figure 1—right) and absence of both Achilles tendon reflexes. plate_findings.evidence: In-text: 'Clusters and sheets of xanthomatous macrophages were present within the submucosa and infiltrated the lymphoid parenchyma... (Fig. 1)'; low-power view shows pale xanthomatous infiltrates within the lymphoid parenchyma.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Low-power histology of Patient 1's tonsillectomy specimen showing relative preservation of follicular architecture with follicular hyperplasia and pale xanthomatous macrophage infiltrates; caption and in-text attribute these findings to Tangier disease. B: High-power histology showing clusters and sheets of xanthomatous (foam) macrophages infiltrating the tonsillar lymphoid parenchyma, explicitly described in the caption as a hallmark finding in Tangier disease.
